extracted.intended_audience: general wartime newspaper readers and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Associated Press wartime dispatches and short news items (battle reports, refugee conference coverage, domestic wartime developments) intended for general newspaper readership during WWII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to U.S. immigration law when granting asylum
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary of State Hull warned that 'in affording asylum to refugees * * * (the United States) Government is, and must be, bound by legislation enacted by the Congress, determining the immigration policy of the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refugee havens or programs involving entry to the United States must comply with existing U.S. immigration legislation; governmental asylum decisions are constrained by Congress-made immigration policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa eligibility barrier for indigent refugees
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative Sol Bloom pointed out most refugees were indigent, or nearly so, and so not eligible for permanent visas for entry into the United States; legislative action to provide for their support would be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent visa eligibility typically requires financial means or sponsorship; large-scale admission of indigent refugees would require new legislation or support measures to make them eligible for permanent entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal constraints on the use of floating naval mines
rubrics_metrics.description: A floating mine can be used legally only against a specific objective such as an enemy ship or ships and must be adjusted so that it will become harmless within twenty-four hours after it is released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under international law (as described in the article) floating mines are legally restricted: they must target specific objectives and be set to become harmless within 24 hours; this contrasts with anchored mines and limits indiscriminate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: British White Paper (May 1939) limit on Jewish immigration to Palestine
rubrics_metrics.description: The British White Paper of May, 1939 limited Jewish immigration into Palestine from that time to about 30,000 and bars immigration after 30,000; transfer of large numbers of refugees to Palestine would necessarily abrogate those terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any plan to send substantial numbers of refugees to Palestine would conflict with existing British policy (the 1939 White Paper) and would require abrogation or alteration of that policy to be implemented.
